title: Best before bedtime.
subject: PNN: Cookie-led alien abductions are up. A study, with travel statistics, from a team that was in two places at once.
preheader: A UFO, a plate of cookies, and an alibi hundreds of miles long. Statistics included.

featuredCase.teaser: **Aliens landed in Anaheim. A yard back home was abducted the same day.** The Area 51 Bureau met the pink team at a theme park, learned its travel plans, and visited a pink lawn with cookies, a foil flagship, and a cow. Clueso has the file. *Whether the cookies were only cookies is now a matter of public speculation.*
featuredCase.hook: including a suspect sketch and a flagship made of an umbrella

sections.kicker: SPECIAL REPORT / THE DEPARTMENT OF INTERSTELLAR SNACK LOGISTICS
sections.heading:
Cookie-led abductions: a study in soft landings.
(Easy to eat. Easy to miss. Easier to explain.)

runs.text: The
Institute for Alarming Conclusions
reviewed 1,200 reported abductions in which first contact was a plate of baked goods, which is to say it read the same four reports 300 times and asked for seconds.
The findings are in. The cookie is
the oldest tool in the contact kit.
It needs
no translation, no permit, and no explanation of intent.
No species on record has turned down a warm plate on the first approach, and three have asked for the recipe.
Researchers identified the three stages of the method.
Stage one: the plate.
It arrives foil-sealed, warm, and carrying a note.
Stage two: the second helping.
Recipients describe themselves as
comfortable, grateful, and wonderfully unalarmed.
Stage three: the landing.
A flagship touches down on the lawn and the household reports
a very calm evening.
Researchers call this 'the soft landing.' Households call it 'a really nice night.'
A case study is on file. In
the Area 51 Bureau bribed
three households
with cookies before a raid, then landed a foil-hatted flagship on the one it had softened up.
It is the longest pre-landing snack campaign on record. The Institute has asked for the snack budget. The Bureau has asked for confidentiality.
The method has one known flaw.
The household noticed the crash site by morning.
The Institute classifies this as
a slow-acting recipe,
or
a fast-acting cow.
The Institute has recommended further testing, with cookies.
The Institute's final recommendation:
accept the cookies.
Then
read the note.
Then
check the lawn.
In that order.
The pink team has been informed and is already thinking about the ice cream.

sections.heading: The numbers, such as they are

items.text: **Alien contacts that begin with baked goods.** The other 27% begin with *a clipboard, a map, or a very confident question about your cow.*
**Households that notice a UFO on the lawn before the second cookie.** The fifth was *on the second cookie, and has asked to be called back.*
**Aliens turned away at the door by a warm plate.** *The plate has an excellent record. The door has a worse one.*
**The theme-park time warp, per the witness.** Ten seconds felt like forty minutes. *A line at an actual attraction usually runs the other way, with a snack.*
**Pink households bribed before the raid.** Pranked: **one.** Caught: **zero.** *A perfect record in bribes, and a zero in catches.*
**Yards raided in one night by a team that had toured a theme park that day.** Cookies per yard: *undisclosed.* **Cows per yard: at least one.**
**Propulsion of the Bureau's flagship, per its own photograph.** Range: *the length of a lawn.* Alibi range: **hundreds of miles.**
**UFOs that stay up for the whole photo.** The pole is doing all the flying. *It has asked for hazard pay.*
**Teams approached by aliens, by name, on a train platform.** It is the team Clueso is investigating. *That is either bias or a very good source. Clueso declines to say which.*
**Neon-green caution tape that arrives yellow.** The other 12% arrives *backward, which is how the Bureau got its 'NOITUAC.'*
**Times a household has asked 'how did you get here?' after a good cookie.** *It is, in the Institute's view, the most successful question never asked.*

runs.text: Lead finding:
the shortest distance between two places is
a cookie.
The longest is
a rumor with a spaceship in it.
PNN's editors checked the flagship's range three times. It is still a lawn.
The photo is on file as
Exhibit C

sections.heading:
Two places, one day.
(Methods of same-day travel, ranked by plausibility.)

runs.text: A suspect was
at a California theme park by day
and
on a lawn back home by night.
Clueso has questions. The Bureau has a cow.
PNN's Alibi Desk has ranked the possible explanations:
01 / The spaceship.
A pink member's own theory, delivered by text:
'Must have used the spaceship. Only explanation.'
Plausibility: high. The spaceship is an umbrella in a foil hat, but PNN respects the commitment.
02 / The time warp.
The train ride took
ten seconds and forty minutes
at once.
That is plenty of time for a flight, a lunch, and a lawn.
03 / The cookies.
A household with a warm plate in hand is
too comfortable to ask how the Bureau got there.
The cookie covers the route, the timeline, and the cow.
04 / Two Bureaus.
One at the park. One on the lawn.
The Bureau's patch appears to show three aliens, which is more than enough staff for a decoy, a flagship, and a cow.
05 / A very long drive.
PNN's least favorite theory, because it involves
gas stations.
No UFO has ever been refueled at a gas station. The Bureau has not confirmed this.
Clueso has asked for the Bureau's
mileage log, boarding passes, and receipt for the foil.
The Bureau has replied that the foil is classified.

sections.heading:
Are you being abducted by cookies?
(Probably not. Possibly. Keep reading.)

runs.text: 01 / A warm plate appeared and you didn't ask who made it.
The foil was a clue.
The note was a bigger one.
02 / You never asked what the plate was for.
Plates are never just plates. They are an opening move with frosting.
03 / You had a second cookie before you checked the lawn.
This is
how the soft landing works.
PNN is not saying anything. PNN is saying 'check the lawn.'
04 / Your yard now has a cow you did not order.
It has
paw prints
on it.
Clueso notes the paw prints. He notes everything. He has a drawer.
05 / You described the evening as 'unusually peaceful.'
That is the phrase on file for every soft landing in history.
Scoring:
any number of checks means
you are a candidate.
A candidate for what, PNN will let the Bureau explain.
Check the lawn, read the note, and keep the foil.
Preferably have the pink team check it for you,
which has already checked the lawn, the porch, and the cookie.
LOST:
About forty minutes. Last seen on a theme-park train.
If found, return to the witness, who has been asking.
FOR SALE:
One
patio umbrella
, lightly flown. Foil hat included.
Hovering not guaranteed. Attached, however, is.
FOUND:
One cow wearing paw prints.
Claims to be innocent. Clueso is not convinced.
WANTED:
Neon-green caution tape.
Must be green. Must read forward.
NOTICE:
The Crimson Crew's treasure is
deep-frozen,
per the Bureau.
The Crew is accepting offers on one pirate ship, to be named, ideally something with fewer puns.

sections.kicker: A NOTE FROM THE VERIFICATION DESK
sections.heading:
Hospitality tips, from a team that met aliens and sent them the website.
(Same team. Same cat. Still not caught.)

runs.text: PNN's Independent Verification Desk, six inches from Clueso's chair, wishes to note that the
[Prowling Purrpetrators](https://purrpetrators.net/teams/pink/)
were approached by name,
invited the Bureau back for pink starburst and a witch question,
and
suggested it read PNN in line.
Clueso considers this suspicious. The Desk considers it 'a model of hospitality.'
Clueso's three tips for receiving a plate of cookies from an alien:
1 / Check the plate for a forwarding address.
A plate with a return address is a gift. A plate without one is a lawn.
2 / Count the cows.
One is decoration. Two is a herd. Three is a statement.
3 / Keep pranks clever, kind, and away from sleep and young children (rules 6 and 7).
A UFO on a lawn is a joke. A wake-up call is not. Photo proof goes to the game group by October 22.
And remember the cookies.
They are evidence. They should be consumed in the line of duty.
PNN will not be taking questions about the ice cream.
Everyone knows the ice cream was freeze-dried. Nobody knows where it went. It has not been seen since the thread.
